title: Agilent to buy pathology software maker Proscia for $240 million
source_used: HIT Consultant (account of Agilent's announcement of 13 Oct 2026); Reuters headline seen but article blocked
key_facts: Agilent Technologies announced a definitive agreement to acquire Proscia, a digital pathology software and AI company (13 Oct 2026).
Price: $240 million in cash at closing plus up to $30 million more tied to future operational and financial milestones, up to $270 million in total.
Agilent and Proscia signed a multi-year global distribution agreement in September 2022 to co-market an open digital pathology system.

Proscia's Concentriq software is described as deployed in more than 4,000 laboratories, hospital systems and clinics in North America and Europe and as supporting work for 16 of the top 20 pharmaceutical companies.
HIT Consultant says Proscia's trailing twelve-month revenue is above $18 million and that it holds US FDA 510(k) clearance for primary clinical diagnosis.
Agilent chief executive Padraig McDonnell is quoted: the acquisition 'meaningfully expands our presence in this fast-growing market'.
The deal is a signed agreement; the $240 million is payable at closing, so it has not yet closed.
quote_evidence: Analytical and clinical laboratory technology giant Agilent Technologies Inc. announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire digital pathology software and AI company Proscia®.
an all-cash acquisition valued at $240M in cash at closing, plus up to an additional $30M contingent on achieving future operational and financial performance milestones
Agilent and Proscia originally entered into a multi-year global distribution agreement in September 2022
why_it_matters_hint: A laboratory-equipment maker is buying the software that labs use to manage and analyse digital pathology slides, tying AI image analysis to its tissue-testing products.
